q: 1. Who was awarded the Nobel Prize in Medicine in 2026?
options: Robert E. Hall (USA) and Michael Woodford (USA)
Karl Deisseroth (American neuroscientist), Peter Hegemann (Germany) and Georg Nagel (Germany)
Henri B. Kagan (France) and Kenso Soai (Japan)
explain: The prize was awarded for discoveries on light-sensitive ion channels and optogenetics. With it, scientists can send special light into a living brain to switch a particular cell on (activate) or off (deactivate) at will. It has brought a new revolution in neuroscience, and the technology is expected to play a major role in finding treatments for Parkinson's, Alzheimer's and other complex mental and neurological diseases.

q: 2. In which sports did Nepal manage to win medals at the 20th Asian Games, 2026?
options: Women's Kabaddi (1 bronze) and Karate (Tenzing Sherpa, 1 bronze)
explain: The Games were held in Nagoya, Japan from 19 September to 4 October 2026. Slogan: Imagine One Asia. 45 nations (including one Asian Refugee Team), 10,787 athletes and 43 sports took part. In the medal table, China was first (169 gold, 89 silver, 83 bronze, total 341), Japan second (83, 95, 91, total 269) and South Korea third (39, 43, 68, total 150). Nepal's flag at the march-past was carried by national women's kabaddi player Manpati Bista and boxer Chandra Bahadur Thapa Magar. This was the third time Japan hosted the Asian Games (earlier in Tokyo in 1958 and Hiroshima in 1994).

q: 3. How many bird species are currently recorded in Nepal?
explain: The 904th species is the Collared Kingfisher. It was first seen at Janakpurdham, Dhanusha on B.S. 2083 Asoj 13. It is found mainly in coastal areas. Scientific name: Todiramphus chloris. The species is found mainly in South Asia, Southeast Asia, Australia and Pacific coastal regions, and its nearest permanent habitat is West Bengal in India and the Sundarbans of Bangladesh. Ornithologists estimate that in Nepal it arrived by wandering along the Ganga–Brahmaputra river system or by losing its way due to weather.

q: 4. To which post was Nepal elected at the 11th Annual Meeting of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB)?
explain: The meeting held in Doha, the capital of Qatar, on 28–29 September 2026 elected Nepal as Vice President from among regional member countries for 2026–27. Nepal, a founding member of the bank, was elected to this post for the first time from among regional members. As the bank provides for one President and one Vice President each from regional and non-regional members, Ireland (from non-regional members) was also selected along with Nepal this time.

q: 5. Who is the Nepali appointed as head of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) South Asia Regional Office and Innovation Centre in New Delhi?
explain: Nepali telecommunication and information technology expert Anandraj Khanal has been appointed to the post. Appointed on 22 September 2026, Khanal took charge on 1 October 2026. The jurisdiction of this regional office, established in cooperation with the Government of India, includes Nepal, Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Iran, Maldives and Sri Lanka.

q: 6. Which Nepali documentary won the Special Jury Short Documentary Award at the 12th International Films Festival, 2026, held in Shimla, India?
explain: Directed by journalist Ganesh Pandey, the film achieved this success while competing with international documentaries from 33 countries. It captures the adventurous journey to Everest Base Camp of people with serious brain injuries (brain injury survivors) and the story of their struggle. Earlier, the documentary had won the Best Documentary Film Award at the 'Kab' International Film Festival in the USA.

q: 7. What is the Baby Boom related to?
options: A surge in the birth of children
explain: Shortly after the Second World War ended, from 1948 onwards, an unprecedented number of children were born worldwide, at a rate never seen before. Demographers called this event of rising births the 'Baby Boom'. It lasted about 12 years, until 1960. The baby boom was greatest especially in the post-war regions of Europe, America, Japan and Korea.

q: 8. Who is the activist who led the 'Chipko Movement' for environmental conservation?
explain: He led this movement around 1973 against deforestation in the Garhwal region of India.

q: 9. How many points does the declaration made public by the 'Women Leadership Summit 2026', held in Koshi Province, contain?
explain: The 'Women Leadership Summit 2026' (B.S. 2083 Baisakh), organized in Biratnagar, Koshi Province, concluded after in-depth discussion on women's leadership, entrepreneurship and economic participation, issuing a 16-point declaration. Entrepreneurs and stakeholders, rather than limiting women to the workforce, stressed skill development, financial access and mentorship to bring them to leadership levels, and pledged to increase women's employment in their organizations.

q: 10. Who is the player who set the record of winning a gold medal at the youngest age in the history of the Asian Games?
options: Yuki Kurihara (11 years, Japan), 20th Asian Games, 2026
explain: Yuki Kurihara, an 11-year-old primary school student from Japan, became the youngest gold medalist at the Asian Games (in 'Puyo Puyo' under e-sports). Kurihara defeated 28-year-old Tanarak Wongkitkun of Thailand in the semi-final and 24-year-old Kang Dohsin of South Korea in the final. He had secured his place to represent Japan at the Asian Games at just 10 years old, and achieved this success while balancing school, extra classes and training. According to the Olympic Council of Asia, Kurihara's win is the record for the youngest gold medal winner in Asian Games history.

q: 11. Who is, by provision, the convener of the Local Revenue Advisory Committee formed in a municipality?
explain: The Deputy Mayor of the municipality is provided to be the convener of the Local Revenue Advisory Committee formed in a municipality.

q: 12. Who is the mountaineer who succeeded in climbing all 14 mountains in the world above eight thousand meters at the youngest age and entering the Guinness Book of World Records?
explain: Mingma, who first climbed Manaslu in 2022, achieved this feat by 2024.

q: 13. When is Civil Security Day observed in Nepal?
explain: Civil Security Day is observed in Nepal on Asoj 12, and it has been observed since B.S. 2068.

q: 14. When was the National Transport Policy, 2083 approved?
explain: With the approval of the new Transport Policy, 2083, the long-standing National Transport Policy, 2058 has automatically been repealed. The new policy mentions adopting PPP and other suitable models to promote private sector participation in the development of public transport and road infrastructure. Funds received from climate finance, green investment and carbon crediting will be mobilized with priority for developing infrastructure and expanding the system for electric vehicles. To make transport management effective, priority has been given to the Intelligent Transport System (ITS), smart payment systems, and women-, child-, senior citizen- and disability-friendly design principles.

q: 15. Which portal has been brought into operation to make import-export work easy?
options: Nepal Trade (brought into operation by the Government of Nepal)
explain: The 'Nepal Trade' portal has been brought into operation by the Government of Nepal to make import-export work easy.

q: 16. When is International Day of Older Persons observed?
explain: The United Nations passed a proposal on 14 December 1990 to observe 1 October as the International Day of Older Persons. On 1 October 2026, the 36th International Day was observed.

q: 17. When did the US-led coalition formally end its military mission and withdraw from Iraq?
explain: Analysts hold that the coalition forces' exit ends the power that balanced Tehran's influence in Iraq since the stay began, and that Iran gains a strategic advantage. With Iraq not yet fully ready to take over security, it is noted that the US withdrawal creates a vacuum and carries the risk of reviving extremist groups such as the Islamic State.
